A.why: Plum-brown ground under a violet-slate far land is unlike anything else in the run, but the grey-violet road sits close in value to the plum ground at eye level.
A.fix: road cobblestone about 12 values lighter and a touch cooler so it parts from the plum walk ground at eye level

B.why: The pale path reads well from above, but olive moss ground with a grey road is nearly the same picture as D and E and the moor, and the 'snow' path is warm grey, not snow.
B.fix: road snow 15 values lighter and cooler (blue-white grey) so the first snow, not the moss, defines the place

C.why: Warm rust spoil against a cool grey-green track gives a clear hue split and the verdigris says copper, though the warm ground is a little light and the far land is the same brown as the walk.
C.fix: far slate shifted cool grey (toward the slag) so walkable rust and far land part, and walk ground 6 values darker

D.why: Green-black ground with pale limestone and a clear grey road reads, but without water it is a dark green field near B and E, and the ochre accent reads more mustard than stained glass.
D.fix: walk mud 6 values darker and greener-black so the marsh separates from B and E, and accent nudged toward warmer amber-gold

E.why: The will-o'-wisp blue is a good accent, but the 'near-black peat' renders as mid olive almost identical to B, so it never reads as bog.
E.fix: walk ground 15 values darker and browner (true peat) so the pale causeway and grey stones stand out of it

F.why: The turquoise tile accent is clear and lovely against warm ground, but the 'red clay' renders mauve-brown close to A and C and the sand road is only a step above it.
F.fix: walk sand and rock pushed redder (more rust, less mauve) and the road 10 values lighter toward pale wash sand

G.why: Dark loam with a pale flagstone road reads best of the run from every camera, the violet far rim and pale-violet light give it a place of its own, and it is properly dark and matte.
G.fix: walk leafygrass 5 values darker and slightly more umber so the deepwood floor feels closed-in and the violet glow carries more

H.why: The inverted value plan (pale ground, dark trodden road) is unmistakable and reads clearly, but the plain is khaki-olive rather than bleached bone and edges toward washed out, and the dusk-rose is a bit soft.
H.fix: walk sand desaturated and cooled toward grey-white bone (less olive) while keeping its value, so it reads as bone dust not dry grass

notes: Judged from images only. The run splits into a warm-brown cluster (A, C, F) and an olive-green cluster (B, D, E) that are hard to tell apart at night; G and H escape by value plan (G's dark loam and pale road, H's inverted pale ground and dark road) and by a non-amber light or far land. Several palettes (B, E, F) render lighter or less saturated than their descriptions promise: 'near-black', 'snow' and 'red' all got lost. Water roles requested by D and E would help that cluster most.
